name: hot-bag
description: Keep an Apple Silicon Mac running an unattended job lid-closed in a bag: `start` flips `pmset disablesleep` behind a typed-yes /dev/tty gate (headless callers stage it for `toolbelt approve`), a sudo-free watchdog logs temperature/battery/tether every 30s, `off` restores sleep ungated, a menu-bar icon shows on/wedged
hits: this Mac's power management (`pmset disablesleep`) + thermal/battery/tether telemetry
surface: CLI. `status`/`report` are free. `start`/`on` previews the plan and takes a typed "yes" on /dev/tty before `sudo pmset -a disablesleep 1`; there is no --yes; with no terminal it stages and prints `toolbelt approve hot-bag <code>`. `stop`/`off` and `doctor` restore sleep and are deliberately ungated. The watchdog's exit trap attempts a passwordless restore and audits the outcome; every pmset mutation is one line in ~/.local/state/hot-bag/audit.log

origin.note: personal repo by the belt owner. Vendored via git archive; hot-bag-graphic.png (3.5 MB README art) was dropped after the copy. The belt copy adds the /dev/tty gate, staging + approve, the audit log and the watchdog restore trap; the origin has none of these

env.name: HOTBAG_HOME
env.description: State dir: runs/*.csv, pid files, disablesleep.on marker, pending/ staging queue, audit.log. Default ~/.local/state/hot-bag. The smoke test points it at a temp dir

env.name: INTERVAL
env.description: Seconds between telemetry samples (default 30). Also settable in ~/.config/hot-bag/config with WARN_C/HOT_C/CRIT_C/PING_HOST/LOW_BATT_ACTION/LID_CHIME*

env.name: WIFI_SSID
env.description: Optional hotspot to rejoin when the link drops; blank disables the rejoin

env.name: WIFI_PASSWORD
env.description: Password for WIFI_SSID. Set it in ~/.config/hot-bag/config (chmod 600), never in a shell rc; it is passed to networksetup on argv only when a rejoin fires

auth.flow: the operator's own admin rights: `sudo pmset` prompts for their password at the terminal (on managed Macs `ensure_admin` first offers a Privileges.app elevation, also confirmed at /dev/tty). No token, no cache, nothing to revoke

safeguards: start/on is gated on /dev/tty: the plan (the exact `sudo pmset -a disablesleep 1`, the restore verb, the worst case) is printed and the operator types "yes" at the controlling terminal — `tty_read` in hot-bag opens /dev/tty directly, never stdin, so `echo yes | hot-bag start` does not pass; then sudo's own prompt follows (SENSIBILITIES #2)

start takes no --yes/--force: either is a usage error (exit 2). A sudo ticket cached from an earlier command would otherwise let a headless caller flip the override with no human in the loop; the typed yes is what makes it a human's act

start with no controlling terminal STAGES instead of refusing: a 600-mode record under $HOTBAG_HOME/pending/<code> (dir 700, 15-minute expiry, pruned on every touch), exit 2, and the one command printed — `toolbelt approve hot-bag <code>`. Nothing is changed until a human confirms (`stage_start`, `approve` in hot-bag)

approve opens /dev/tty — never stdin — shows the same plan, takes a typed yes, deletes the record (single use) and runs start in-process through `_HB_APPROVED`, a shell variable reset to 0 at script load so no environment value can pre-approve; with no terminal it refuses (exit 1) and keeps the record, never re-stages or auto-approves

The restore path is ungated and un-bypassable on purpose: stop/off runs `pmset -a disablesleep 0` first, does not abort cleanup if sudo fails, and exits non-zero so a still-on override is loud; doctor restores only when the disablesleep.on marker proves hot-bag set it (never an override something else set)

Degraded mode: start arms a trap (INT TERM HUP EXIT) that restores sleep if it aborts after the override was set; the watchdog (_watch) arms a trap that attempts `sudo -n pmset -a disablesleep 0` on any exit and audits `restored` or `not-restored(no passwordless sudo)` — the wedged state is then visible in status, the menu-bar ⚠️, and the doctor's sleep-state check (SENSIBILITIES #8)

Every pmset mutation goes through one function (`pmset_disablesleep`) that appends `[hot-bag audit] <ts> verb= target= result=` to $HOTBAG_HOME/audit.log and stderr; staging, approve, decline, discard and the watchdog's exit attempt are audited too (SENSIBILITIES #7)
start --explain prints the plan and touches nothing: no ping, no sudo, no state file (SENSIBILITIES #5)

No bare `pkill caffeinate`: only processes verified by pid AND command line (`safe_ps_match`) are killed; foreign caffeinate sessions are reported, and swept only under the explicit `stop --kill-stray-caffeinate`

The watchdog is sudo-free by design: no telemetry reader needs a password, so the unattended loop has no credential dependency; the only sudo calls are the foreground pmset in start/stop/doctor and the opt-in `sudo -n` safeties (low battery, exit trap)
No secret in the tree: the one credential-shaped setting (WIFI_PASSWORD) lives in ~/.config/hot-bag/config outside the repo; config.example is vendored, the real file never is (SENSIBILITIES #11)

verbs.name: status
verbs.note: one-shot live reading: override on/off, temps, throttle, battery, link, data this run; warns on a wedged state. One ping to PING_HOST

verbs.name: report
verbs.note: summary + verdict over a run CSV (default: current or latest)

verbs.name: chime
verbs.note: plays the lid-close chime once; if the Mac is muted and LID_CHIME_UNMUTE=on it unmutes for the ~0.5s tone and restores the exact prior mute/volume

verbs.name: start --explain
verbs.note: the pre-flight: prints the plan, changes nothing

verbs.name: _indicator-state
verbs.note: internal: on|wedged|off for the menu-bar icon; no ping, no sudo

verbs.name: start
verbs.note: alias `on`. `sudo pmset -a disablesleep 1` + watchdog + caffeinate: system state that must be restored. Typed yes on /dev/tty then sudo's prompt; no --yes; headless → staged (exit 2) for `toolbelt approve hot-bag <code>`

verbs.name: approve
verbs.note: what `toolbelt approve hot-bag <code>` runs: shows the plan, typed yes on /dev/tty, runs start once, deletes the record; no terminal → refuse, record kept

verbs.name: stop
verbs.note: alias `off`. The restore path: `pmset -a disablesleep 0`, kill our watchdog/caffeinate/lid-watcher, print the report. Deliberately ungated — a gate on restoring normal sleep would be a gate on safety; sudo still prompts. `--kill-stray-caffeinate` additionally kills OTHER caffeinate processes (reported, never swept, without the flag)

verbs.name: doctor
verbs.note: recovery: restores sleep only if hot-bag's disablesleep.on marker exists, sweeps only verified-ours processes, removes stale pid/lock files. Ungated for the same reason as stop; refuses to clear an override hot-bag did not set

verbs.name: _watch
verbs.note: internal sampling loop spawned by start; writes runs/*.csv under HOTBAG_HOME; exit trap attempts the passwordless restore

verbs.name: _lidwatch
verbs.note: internal: chimes on lid close while the watchdog lives

verbs.name: any other pmset setting (hibernatemode, autopoweroff, …)
verbs.note: the code touches exactly one key, disablesleep; nothing else is reachable

risk.worst_case: disablesleep stays at 1 after a crash with no passwordless sudo: the lid-closed Mac keeps running hot in a zipped bag until the battery is flat or `hot-bag off` / `hot-bag doctor` restores sleep — the wedged state is visible in status, the doctor and the menu-bar ⚠️, and the audit log names the failed restore attempt
